title: Ensure Windows Firewall is enabled for Domain profile
description: The Windows Firewall Domain profile should be enabled to filter inbound traffic on domain networks.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-FW-001 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Enable Windows Firewall for the Domain profile via Group Policy or Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain -Enabled True.

title: Ensure Windows Firewall is enabled for Private profile
description: The Windows Firewall Private profile should be enabled to filter inbound traffic on private networks.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-FW-002 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Enable Windows Firewall for the Private profile via Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Private -Enabled True.

title: Ensure Windows Firewall is enabled for Public profile
description: The Windows Firewall Public profile should be enabled to filter inbound traffic on public networks.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-FW-003 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Enable Windows Firewall for the Public profile via Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Public -Enabled True.

title: Ensure Windows Defender antivirus is enabled
description: Windows Defender antivirus should be active to detect and remove malware.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-DEF-004 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Enable Windows Defender antivirus. Ensure no conflicting third-party AV has disabled it.

title: Ensure Windows Defender real-time protection is enabled
description: Real-time protection continuously monitors the system for malicious activity.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-DEF-005 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)

title: Ensure Guest account is disabled
description: The Guest account allows unauthenticated access and should be disabled.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-ACC-006 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)

title: Ensure minimum password length is configured
description: Short passwords are vulnerable to brute-force attacks. Minimum length configuration is required.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-PASS-007 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Set minimum password length to 14 or more characters via Group Policy: Account Policies > Password Policy.

title: Ensure account lockout threshold is configured
description: Account lockout prevents brute-force attacks by locking accounts after repeated failed logins.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-PASS-008 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Configure account lockout threshold (e.g. 5 attempts) via Group Policy: Account Lockout Policy.

title: Ensure SMBv1 protocol is disabled
description: SMBv1 is an obsolete and vulnerable protocol exploited by ransomware such as WannaCry and NotPetya.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-SMB-009 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)

title: Ensure RDP requires Network Level Authentication
description: NLA authenticates users before establishing a full RDP session, reducing exposure to unauthenticated connections.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-RDP-010 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Enable NLA for RDP: Set UserAuthentication to 1 in HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp.

title: Ensure Telnet client is not installed
description: Telnet transmits data in plaintext. The Telnet client optional feature should not be installed.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-TEL-011 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Remove the Telnet client: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName TelnetClient.

title: Ensure logon events are audited
description: Auditing logon events provides an audit trail for account-use activity and security incidents.
benchmark_reference: ILLUSTRATIVE-WIN-AUD-012 (custom example rule based on CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2022 Benchmark principles)
remediation: Configure Logon audit policy via auditpol /set /subcategory:'Logon' /success:enable /failure:enable.
